change.title: pr-2-flat
change.description: Optimize spans buffer insertion with eviction during insert
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator treats a datetime key as a number: every non-empty page returns 500
findings.body: The audit log endpoint uses this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`. `get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly on `getattr(item, 'datetime')`. That is a `datetime`, so it raises TypeError the first time `build_cursor` computes a key, which happens on any page with results. `value_from_cursor` also returns the raw cursor number, and `build_queryset` (paginator.py:119-126) then compares it to the datetime column. The paginator it replaces, `DateTimePaginator` (paginator.py:233-241), converts in both directions: `strftime('%s.%f') * 1000` and `datetime.fromtimestamp(value/1000)`. So any admin who sends `optimized_pagination=true` gets a 500, and cursors are not compatible between the two paths. Either subclass DateTimePaginator or reuse its key and value conversion.

findings.title: Negative-offset branch cannot work and is described as reaching data 'beyond normal pagination bounds'
findings.body: Django QuerySets reject negative slice indices with "Negative indexing is not supported.", so `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with `cursor.offset < 0` raises and the request returns a 500. Nothing is paginated. The comments say this is "safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level" and that it "enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds", which describes an intent to bypass bounds. Remove the branch along with `enable_advanced_features`, and reject negative offsets in cursor parsing with a 400.

findings.title: BasePaginator change keeps negative offsets for prev cursors, and its comment is wrong
findings.body: Every paginator that inherits `BasePaginator.get_result` is affected. With `is_prev` set, a client-supplied negative offset (e.g. `cursor=0:-5:1`) still reaches `queryset[offset:stop]`, and Django raises on negative indexing, so the request returns a 500 instead of a 400. Before this change both directions raised the same way. Now only next cursors are clamped. The comment saying "the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions" is false. Clamp in both directions, or raise `BadPaginationError` for `offset < 0`; `paginate` turns that into a ParseError (base.py:540-541).

findings.title: `organization_context.member` can be None, and `is_superuser` ignores whether superuser mode is active
findings.body: For a non-superuser request with no org membership, `organization_context.member` is None, and `.has_global_access` raises AttributeError (I did not confirm that OrganizationAuditPermission lets such requests through, e.g. staff). The check also runs for every request, before `use_optimized` is tested. Evaluate it only when `use_optimized` is true and guard against None. Elsewhere Sentry checks `is_active_superuser(request)` rather than `request.user.is_superuser`. This only matters as long as the optimized path is kept (see the paginator findings).

findings.title: Switching set to sorted-set breaks keys already in Redis during rollout (WRONGTYPE)
findings.body: Before this change, `span-buf:s:*` keys were Redis sets (SADD/SSCAN). After deploy, `zadd` here, `zcard`/`zunionstore` in add-buffer.lua:46-53, and `zscan` at buffer.py:434 all fail with WRONGTYPE on any segment key written by the old code, until those keys expire (`set_timeout`/redis_ttl). An error in the pipeline makes `p.execute()` raise, so the consumer can crash-loop on those batches and the buffered segments are lost. Either use a new key prefix for the zset keys or handle the migration explicitly.

findings.title: Oversized segments are now truncated silently, with no metric or log
findings.body: Before this change, segments over `max_segment_spans` were dropped with the `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded` metric and an error log. Now `zpopmin` throws away the spans with the earliest end timestamps, and nothing records that it happened, so downstream sees incomplete segments with no signal. The limit of 1000 is also hard-coded here, while `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` (buffer.py:150,158) is now never read: it is dead config, and it no longer controls the limit. Pass the limit as an ARGV, and emit a metric or a return value when spans are evicted. Note too that `zunionstore` defaults to SUM, so a duplicate payload ends up with a doubled score.

findings.title: No test for the new 1000-span eviction or for OptimizedCursorPaginator
findings.body: The test changes only add `end_timestamp_precise` to fixtures, all with the same value. No test covers a segment larger than 1000 spans, the order in which spans are evicted, or the new audit-log `optimized_pagination` path. A single endpoint test with that flag would have caught the datetime TypeError.

contracts.action: GET audit logs with optimized_pagination=true as superuser/global-access member
contracts.before_after: DateTimePaginator converts the datetime key to epoch ms and back; OptimizedCursorPaginator does math.floor on the raw datetime and passes the raw cursor value to the SQL filter
contracts.visible_effect: 500 on any non-empty page; negative offsets also give a 500
contracts.failure_mode: TypeError in get_item_key / Django negative-index error, surfaced as an unhandled 500

contracts.action: Store spans in Redis sorted sets scored by end_timestamp_precise, capped at 1000
contracts.equivalent_path: previous SADD/SSCAN path with the max_segment_spans drop
contracts.before_after: before: oversized segments dropped with a metric; after: truncated in Lua with no metric; old set-typed keys are incompatible
contracts.failure_mode: WRONGTYPE errors on keys left over from before the deploy make the pipeline execute raise

summary: The audit-log 'optimized' paginator is broken: it applies math.floor to a datetime, so every non-empty page returns 500, and its negative-offset feature cannot work in Django and is described as bypassing bounds. The BasePaginator negative-offset change is inconsistent and its comment is wrong. In the span buffer, moving from sets to sorted sets makes keys already in Redis fail with WRONGTYPE during rollout, and oversized segments are now truncated without any metric. max_segment_spans is dead config, and there are no tests for the new behaviour.
